rationale:
What went well:
- The agent properly authenticated the user via full name + zip and matched a single account before acting.
- They gathered relevant order details and variants, and the user explicitly specified the desired exchange options for the bicycle and puzzle before the agent proceeded.

Issues leading to fail:
- The agent performed an order-changing write (cancellation) without explicitly confirming the exact change. The user asked to cancel the skateboard item and was okay canceling the whole order only if single-item cancellation wasn’t possible. The agent did not check or attempt item-level cancellation and unilaterally canceled the entire order #W8855135, violating the requirement to confirm the exact change before proceeding.
- The agent stated refund details that were not supported by tool outputs. They asserted the cancellation refund would go to card ending 6791 and in 5–7 business days without verifying the original payment method for that order or any refund timing from tools.
- Earlier, the agent claimed availability and delivery details that weren’t clearly supported by the truncated tool data (e.g., puzzle variant availability and “two delivered orders”), risking fabrication.

Because of the unconfirmed whole-order cancellation and unsupported refund details, the interaction fails the policy requirements for confirmation and accuracy.
